summary:
KAWSAY (Quechua for “life”) is a web-based astronaut health monitoring app for long-duration deep-space missions. It gives crew members a way to autonomously track and document their health without depending on real-time communication with Earth.

The app combines two layers: a passive wearable sensor feed showing HR, SpO₂, temperature, and blood pressure with automated anomaly alerts — and a structured 6-step daily check-in (wellness rating, body map, symptoms, images, notes, and medication log) submitted directly to Ground Control.

The Ground Control dashboard gives mission commanders a real-time crew health overview with amber flags on concerning values. KAWSAY addresses all 5 NASA HRP hazard categories. Built as a single HTML/CSS/JS file with no backend or dependencies — it runs fully offline on any browser-capable device.
details:
What it does

KAWSAY monitors astronaut health through two parallel layers:

Passive layer — Wearable sensors
Each astronaut’s dashboard displays real-time vitals with clinical reference ranges. The app automatically flags readings outside normal bounds and detects discrepancies between sensor data and self-reported wellness, triggering amber alerts for Ground Control.

Active layer — Daily check-in flow (6 steps)

  1. Wellness — Overall rating 1–5
  2. Body Map — Click to locate pain or discomfort
  3. Symptoms — Select from a curated list
  4. Images — Upload photos of injuries or anomalies
  5. Notes — Free-text narrative for the flight physician
  6. Medications — Log dosage, timing, and adherence

After submission, the app delivers personalized health guidance to the astronaut, closing the loop.

Ground Control (SGC) dashboard
Accessible via PIN 0000. Commanders see the full crew status across all active missions, with real-time vitals and amber flags on elevated values. Each astronaut’s check-in history is available for review.

Why this matters
On a Mars mission, astronauts face an 11.5-minute one-way communication delay and no emergency evacuation option. KAWSAY gives them a structured tool to monitor, document, and understand their own health — and gives Ground Control the data they need for proactive intervention, even across the communication gap.

Tech stack
Pure HTML / CSS / JavaScript — single-file application
No backend, no server, no dependencies
LocalStorage for offline persistence
Google Fonts (DM Sans)
Deployed on Vercel
